Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma · public GEO data · R-CHOP-treated cohorts

DLBCL Prognostic Score

A 44-gene elastic-net Cox score for overall survival, trained on one cohort and tested under an analysis plan that was written and hash-locked before any test data were opened. This page shows the validation, the controls, the comparison with IPI and cell of origin, and the biology the score picks up.

Research only.This is not a diagnostic or treatment tool. The score is standardised within each cohort, so it cannot be applied to an individual new patient, and no result here supports a clinical decision.

Pre-specified conclusions

What held up, and how strongly

The three conclusion sentences were fixed in the analysis plan before the test set was opened. Each row gives the evidence behind the label, including where it is weaker than the label suggests.

Study design

One cohort to build, three to test

GSE181063 (Illumina DASL, FFPE) was split 70/30 before any analysis. All modelling choices were made on the training part. The test part and two Affymetrix cohorts, GSE10846 and GSE87371, were opened once, in that order, after the plan was locked.

Numbers behind these charts

All three validation C-indices sit a little above the training estimate (+0.02 to +0.05). Every interval contains 0.61, so chance in sets of 41–74 deaths is the simplest explanation. Read the intervals, not the point values.

Step 5 · negative control and leakage check

Shuffled survival labels give nothing

The whole pipeline, including cross-validated penalty selection, was re-run 100 times on training data with survival times and events shuffled together. Each permutation model was then scored on the real test labels.

Step 8 · exploratory, training set only

The score mostly rediscovers known DLBCL biology

Higher scores go with proliferation, MYC targets and the ABC/IRF4 program; lower scores with extracellular-matrix, stromal and T-cell genes. This matches Rosenwald 2002 and Lenz 2008. No hypothesis was tested here, and p-values are descriptive.

Hallmark gene sets vs the score
Higher with higher scoreHigher with lower scoreNot robustGene-sampling z. "Robust" = FDR < 0.05 in both the permutation and the gene-sampling test. Model genes removed from the universe.
Known signatures vs the score (Spearman ρ, 95% CI)
Signature score = mean gene z-score. Stromal entries are Hallmark proxies, not the Lenz 2008 lists.

A contradiction we cannot resolve: Lenz 2008 linked the stromal-2 (angiogenesis) signature to poor outcome, but our angiogenesis proxy goes with the low-risk side. The proxy overlaps with matrix genes, so stromal-1 and stromal-2 cannot be separated here. Together, six signatures explain about 35% of the score's variance; the rest is not explained by them.

Frozen model · 44 genes

Individual genes are unstable; the score as a whole is what was validated

Only 4 of the 44 genes were selected in at least half of 100 bootstrap refits. Treat the list as one possible sparse solution, not as 44 findings.

Coefficient: log hazard ratio per training SD of expression. Symbols: current GPL570 annotation; matching was done by Entrez ID.

Limitations

  • No clinical use. Within-cohort z-scoring means absolute risk and cut-offs do not transfer; there is no external calibration and no decision-curve analysis.
  • The "adds information" label rests on a weak external condition. It required only a point estimate above 1 in the external cohorts; both intervals include 1 and both likelihood-ratio tests are non-significant.
  • The internal test set shares cohort, platform, laboratory and COO classifier with training. H3 was met only there.
  • Missing IPI. Complete-case analysis drops 36 test and 75 GSE10846 patients; in the test set, patients with missing IPI died more often (55.6% vs 42.9%, log-rank p = 0.074).
  • Small external cohorts. GSE87371 has 41 deaths; excluding 13 R-mini-CHOP21 patients moves its HR to 1.39 (0.98–1.96). GSE10846 has a median follow-up of 34 months.
  • Processed GEO values were used, not re-processed CEL files; pre-processing differs between cohorts.
  • Pre-registration is internal. The plan was hash-locked on Google Drive before the test set was opened, but not deposited with an external registry or timestamping service, so the order of events is documented, not independently provable.
  • Modest novelty. The contribution is a transparent, fully logged workflow, not new biology. No head-to-head comparison with published DLBCL signatures was done.
Data: GEO series GSE181063 (Lacy et al. 2020; Painter et al. 2019), GSE10846 and GSE87371 (Dubois et al. 2017). Public, de-identified data. This page is built only from summary results in the repository. It contains no patient-level records; the survival curves are aggregate Kaplan–Meier step functions.
